title: CBFC Clears Awarapan 2 With U/A 16+ Certificate and Minimal Cuts Ahead of Independence Day Release
excerpt: The censor board passed the Emraan Hashmi-Disha Patani sequel with targeted cuts to violence and drug scenes, certifying it at 2 hours 20 minutes for its August 14 theatrical release.
body:
• The CBFC passed Awarapan 2 with a U/A 16+ certificate on August 5, clearing it for its August 14 theatrical release
  • Cuts included a 50% reduction in one violent scene, deletion of three extreme violence sequences, and removal of a drug snorting scene
  • The certified runtime is 140 minutes and 20 seconds — making it the only non-adult-rated film among major August releases
  • The film stars Emraan Hashmi returning as Shivam Pandit opposite Disha Patani and Shabana Azmi, directed by Nitin Kakkar

The Central Board of Film Certification has cleared Awarapan 2 with a U/A 16+ certificate, removing the last regulatory hurdle before the Emraan Hashmi-starrer's worldwide theatrical release on August 14. The censor certificate was issued on August 5, confirming a final runtime of 140 minutes and 20 seconds, Bollywood Hungama reported exclusively.

What the CBFC Cut

The examining committee asked for a focused set of modifications. Makers were required to add disclaimers for the depiction of drug use and child trafficking, along with an anti-smoking ticker. As per regulations in effect since 2021, the film title was required to appear in Hindi.

An anti-drug static ticker was ordered for the bottom right corner during scenes of drug consumption. Obscene words in both audio and subtitles were replaced with approved alternatives.

The more substantive cuts targeted violence. In the second half, one violent scene was reduced by 50%. Three additional scenes depicting extreme violence were deleted outright. A scene showing drug snorting at the film's midpoint was also removed.

The modifications are considered minimal by industry standards. The U/A 16+ certificate — rather than a full 'A' (adults only) rating — gives the film access to a significantly wider audience, a meaningful commercial advantage for the Independence Day release window.

The Only Non-Adult Film in a Crowded Weekend

Awarapan 2 holds a notable distinction among August's major releases. Bollywood Hungama pointed out that it is the only non-adult-rated film of the season, with competing titles receiving stricter certifications. This positions the Vishesh Films production to draw a broader demographic during the Independence Day weekend, when family audiences typically drive higher footfall.

The film will clash at the box office with War 2, the Hrithik Roshan-Jr NTR action spectacle from Yash Raj Films, which also releases on August 14 with a U/A 16+ certificate but a substantially longer runtime of nearly three hours.

19 Years After the Original

The sequel brings Emraan Hashmi back as Shivam Pandit, the emotionally conflicted gangster he first played in the 2007 original directed by Mohit Suri. That film underperformed at the box office but acquired cult status over the years through its soundtrack — particularly the songs Toh Phir Aao and Tera Mera Rishta — and Hashmi's performance.

"Awarapan is an emotion so large that it's meant for the big screen. Emraan felt the angst of Shivam so deeply that he stepped into character in a heartbeat."

— Vishesh Bhatt, Producer

Disha Patani, fresh from her role in Welcome to the Jungle, joins the franchise for the first time. Veteran actress Shabana Azmi plays what has been described as a powerful negative role. The film is directed by Nitin Kakkar, known for Filmistaan, with a screenplay by Bilal Siddiqui.

Production was completed across Rajasthan, Bangkok, Mumbai, and Malaysia. The music, a critical component of the Awarapan brand, features compositions by Mithoon, Amaal Mallik, Jeet Gannguli, and Akhil Sachdeva, with lyrics by Rashmi Virag and Sayeed Quadri. The track Yeh Awarapan, featuring Arijit Singh, has been positioned as a tribute to the original film's iconic melodies.

Vishesh Films has distributed the film through Pen Marudhar for theatrical release. With nine days until its release date, the censor clearance allows the marketing push to proceed without regulatory uncertainty — a luxury in a season where several competing films have faced protracted censor battles.
nri_angle: The Awarapan franchise holds strong recall value among the Indian diaspora, and the August 14 release during the Independence Day weekend positions it as a major draw for overseas theatrical markets.
